Consider the ellipse centered at the origin with horizontal radius $6$ and vertical radius $5,$ as shown above. Construct a set of parametric equations, defined for $\theta \in [0,2\pi ),$ that traverse the ellipse once in the counterclockwise direction starting at the point $H(6,0).$

{{field-2}}$,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).$
question.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ are

$$
x=a\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=b\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

Under this parametrization, the ellipse is traversed once in the counterclockwise direction, starting from $(a,0).$

In our case, $a=6$ and $b=5.$ Therefore, the parametric equations of the ellipse are

$$
x=6\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=5\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$
